meta.unit: The covenant to the remnant (3 Nephi 20–22)
principles: A sign given so a generation can time the work
A servant protected and marred in the same sentence
Terms offered to the Gentiles in plain conditions

world_behind.title: The sign is a book reaching people
world_behind.text: Verses 2 and 3 make the sign the moment these words are made known to the Gentiles and come from them to the remnant. 2 Nephi 27 and Ether 4:6 describe the same arrival from the other two ends of the record, so three writers a thousand years apart are pointing at one event.

world_behind.title: A political condition is stated
world_behind.text: Verse 4 has the Father give the Gentiles a free footing here, which is what lets the record come out.

world_behind.title: The seed will not be ready to receive it
world_behind.text: Verse 5 says the remnant will have dwindled in unbelief when the record arrives. Ether 4:3 and Mormon 9:35 use the same phrase for what actually happened, so the prediction here and the report four hundred years later are worded alike.

world_behind.title: The work is described before it is named
world_behind.text: Verse 9 calls it a great and marvelous work and says some will not believe it.

world_behind.title: The servant is marred and healed
world_behind.text: Verse 10 says he will not be hurt, then that he will be marred, then that he will be healed. Isaiah 52:14, quoted at 3 Nephi 20:44, has a servant whose visage was so marred more than any man, which is the passage this verse is working from.

world_behind.title: Micah 5 is quoted at length
world_behind.text: Verses 14 to 18 follow Micah 5:10-14 with the list of things cut off.

world_behind.title: The terms are stated twice, both ways
world_behind.text: Verse 20 gives the outcome for those who will not repent and verse 22 gives it for those who will. 3 Nephi 16:13 to 15 had already put the same pair to the same audience, so the visit states the Gentile terms twice in six chapters.

words.text: The scattering of a people. Treated at 2 Nephi 10:8. The record uses the word twice and the King James Bible not at all.
Damaged, spoiled. It appears twice, here and at 3 Nephi 20:44, in the record, and the King James Bible five times. Verse 10 applies it to the servant and promises healing after it.
Wheeled vehicles for war or travel. The record uses the word seven times and the King James Bible one hundred and thirteen. Verse 14 quotes Micah 5:10.
Practices for gaining power by hidden means. The word turns up twice, here and again at Mormon 1:19, here, and the King James Bible four times. Verse 16 quotes Micah 5:12 with soothsayers alongside.
Stands of trees planted at places of worship. The record uses the word once, here, and the King James Bible twenty-four times, mostly in the histories of the kings. Verse 18 quotes Micah 5:14.
Quarrels, contention. Its count is eight times in this book, while the King James Bible four. Verse 19 puts it in a list of six things done away.
Punishment exacted for wrong. The record uses the word thirteen times and the King James Bible forty-five. Verse 21 has the Father execute it as upon the heathen.

phrases.term: I give unto you a sign, that ye may know the time
phrases.text: The sign is for timing. Verse 7 says it tells the seed the work has already begun.

phrases.term: That they may know concerning this people who are a remnant of the house of Jacob
phrases.text: The content of the sign is knowledge about the hearers. What the Gentiles learn is who these people were.

phrases.term: It is wisdom in the Father that they should be established in this land, and be set up as a free people
phrases.text: A condition on the ground stated as the Father's design. Verse 4 gives the reason: the record travels through them to the remnant.

phrases.term: Your seed which shall dwindle in unbelief because of iniquity
phrases.text: The recipients described in advance. The people the record is for will not be looking for it.

phrases.term: If they will not harden their hearts, that they may repent and come unto me
phrases.text: The Gentile terms, stated first as a possibility. Verse 22 will state them again as a promise.

phrases.term: The work of the Father hath already commenced
phrases.text: The sign is a past-tense report. By the time it is recognized the work is underway.

phrases.term: There shall be among them those who will not believe it, although a man shall declare it unto them
phrases.text: Disbelief anticipated inside the prophecy. The declaring and the refusing are named together.

phrases.term: They shall not hurt him, although he shall be marred because of them
phrases.text: Two statements about the servant held in one line. Verse 10 adds the healing and the reason for showing it.

phrases.term: My wisdom is greater than the cunning of the devil
phrases.text: The point of the servant's preservation, stated plainly. The demonstration is the reason given for the whole episode.

phrases.term: They shall come in unto the covenant and be numbered among this the remnant of Jacob
phrases.text: Gentiles entering the covenant on the same terms. Verse 23 has them help build the city.

phrases.term: I will go before them, saith the Father, and I will be their rearward
phrases.text: Isaiah 52:12 with the speaker changed to the Father. 3 Nephi 20:42 had given the same line with the Lord going before.

verses.label: v. 1–7
verses.title: A sign promised twice before it is described
verses.text: The record announces a sign at verse 1, restates the promise at verse 2, "this is the thing which I will give unto you for a sign," and then runs five verses of conditions before the sign itself is finally named at verse 7. Nothing in verses 3 through 6 completes the sentence begun at verse 2; each verse opens with a connective and hands off to the next. The delay is the structure of the passage, and what arrives at the end is not an event in the sky but the appearance of a book among the Gentiles.

verses.label: v. 8
verses.title: A clause reused with its opening line stripped off
verses.text: The record gave all of Isaiah 52:15 a chapter ago, at 3 Nephi 20:45, beginning "So shall he sprinkle many nations." Here the same verse returns without that first clause: "kings shall shut their mouths; for that which had not been told them shall they see; and that which they had not heard shall they consider." The second use keeps the kings and drops the sprinkling. Two uses of one verse, twenty-three verses apart, with the difference confined to the opening line.

verses.label: v. 12–13
verses.title: The same two verses of Micah, now in the third person
verses.text: The record put Micah 5:8–9 at 3 Nephi 20:16–17 addressed to the hearers: "then shall ye, who are a remnant of the house of Jacob, go forth among them," and "Thy hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries." Here the identical material is put in the third person: "my people who are a remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles," and "Their hand shall be lifted up upon their adversaries." The imagery is word for word; only the person changes. The audience is the same in both chapters, so the shift cannot be explained by who is listening.

verses.label: v. 14–18
verses.title: One verb driving five verses
verses.text: The record continues into Micah 5:10–14 and the cutting is counted out item by item: horses, chariots, cities, strongholds, witchcrafts, soothsayers, graven images, standing images, groves. Nine objects across five verses, with "cut off" carrying four of them and destroy, throw down, and pluck up carrying the rest. One small change runs through the block: Micah 5:12 cuts off witchcrafts "out of thine hand," and verse 16 cuts them "out of thy land." The list is otherwise entirely material, running from war horses to carved images, and verse 19 then adds the only non-material entry, lyings and deceivings and envyings and strifes and priestcrafts and whoredoms, in a verse that has no counterpart in Micah at all.

verses.label: v. 29
verses.title: A last line borrowed back from an earlier page
verses.text: Isaiah 52:12 appeared at 3 Nephi 20:42 as "the Lord will go before you, and the God of Israel shall be your rearward." The final verse here renders it "I will go before them, saith the Father, and I will be their rearward." Two divine titles become a first-person pronoun, and an attribution formula is inserted into the middle of the sentence. The record has now quoted Isaiah 52 twice, once with the names intact and once with them replaced, and it does not remark on the difference.

chapter.title: The sign is a book, not an event in the sky
chapter.text: Verses 2 and 3 make the arrival of a record the marker. The timing is given in terms of what people will be reading.

chapter.title: The Gentiles are the carriers
chapter.text: Verse 6 routes it through them so his power is shown to them. Their role in the chapter is delivery.

chapter.title: The recipients are described as unready
chapter.text: Verse 5 says the seed will have dwindled in unbelief. Nothing in the prophecy depends on them expecting it.

chapter.title: The sign is recognized after the fact
chapter.text: Verse 7 says the work has already commenced by the time the seed knows. The chapter builds in a delay.

chapter.title: The servant's protection includes damage
chapter.text: Verse 10 says he will not be hurt and that he will be marred. Both statements stand, with healing given as the resolution.

chapter.title: Micah's list is left mostly intact
chapter.text: Verses 14 to 18 follow Micah 5:10-14 closely. The quotation carries the warning without restatement.

chapter.title: The same offer is made twice
chapter.text: Verse 6 gives the Gentile terms early and verse 22 gives them again after the woes. The chapter closes the door and reopens it in the same speech.

chapter.title: The last word is escort
chapter.text: Verse 29 has the Father before them and behind them. The gathering ends the chapter as a journey under guard.

applications.title: Watch for signs that look like books
applications.text: The marker given here is information reaching people. Some turning points arrive as something to read.

applications.title: Ask what a favorable arrangement is for
applications.text: The verse calls it wisdom in the Father that the Gentiles be established in this land as a free people, so that these things might come forth from them. Advantages are described here as instruments, which is a useful way to hold your own.

applications.title: Expect the work to be underway before you notice it
applications.text: The sign tells the seed what has already started. Recognition and beginning are not the same moment.

applications.title: Some will not believe though a man declare it
applications.text: The prediction attached to a great and marvelous work is that there will be people among them who will not believe it. Expecting unanimity is what makes ordinary disagreement feel like failure.

applications.title: Hold protection and damage together
applications.text: The servant is kept and marred in one sentence. Being preserved is not the same as being spared.

applications.title: Read the list of what stops
applications.text: Lyings, deceivings, envyings, strifes, priestcrafts and whoredoms are named as the things that shall be done away. A picture of a better arrangement is more useful when it says specifically what ends, and this one does.

applications.title: Take the terms as stated
applications.text: Repent, hearken, do not harden. The conditions in this chapter are short and repeated.

applications.title: Assisting is a real assignment
applications.text: Twice the promise is that they shall assist, in building the city and in gathering those who are scattered. Being told your part is assistance is not a demotion, and a great many worthwhile things need exactly that and nothing else.

questions.text: What am I waiting for a sign about?
Where have I dwindled without noticing?
What work is already underway that I have not joined?
What have I refused to believe though someone declared it?
What damage have I taken that was not abandonment?
Which of the six things in this list is still in me?
Where am I moving in haste that I was told not to?
